Taking logs of both sides, this equilibrium relationship can be approximated by it 1⁄4 ptþ1 þ logðzÞ: Now suppose the central bank follows an interest rate rule of the form it 1⁄4 r þ p þ dðpt pÞ; ð10:13Þ where p is the central bank’s target inflation rate and r 1 logðzÞ is the equilibrium rate rate. This policy rule can be viewed as a simple form of the Taylor rule. The Taylor principle calls for ensuring that the nominal interest rate responds more than one-for-one to changes in inflation: d > 1.
